newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks surge as Wall Street soothed by data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks surge as Wall Street soothed by data.

text.p: U.S. stocks rocketed higher on Tuesday in a broad-based rally after economic data soothed Wall Street's concerns over rising interest rates.
The Dow industrials unofficially closed up 179 points, or 2.65 percent, at 6962. It was the blue chip index's second-largest point rise in a single day.
Weaker-than-expected data on wage inflation and orders for manufactured goods on Tuesday coupled with recent strong corporate earnings reports to trigger the surge in share prices, analysts said.
"You've got both portions of the equation working for you today," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer of Value Line's Asset Management.

The Dow's gain topped the 173-point gain posted last Tuesday and fell just short of the all-time record gain of 186.84 points, set on October 21, 1987, two days after the Black Monday crash. In percentage terms, Tuesday's rise was not among the top gainers.
In a sign of the broad participation in the rally, advancing issues on the New York Stock Exchange outnumbered decliners by a four-to-one margin.
The S&P 500 jumped 21 points, or 2.7 percent, to 794. The Nasdaq composite surged 26 points, or 2.1 percent, to 1243.

Stocks rallied from the opening bell, keying on a surging bond market. Analysts said investors took heart in a lower-than-expected rise in the first-quarter Employment Cost Index and an unexpected drop in March durable goods orders.

The data lessened fears that the Federal Reserve would have to raise interest rates significantly to cool the U.S. economy. The Fed raised short-term rates a quarter percentage point on March 25, leading to a monthlong pullback that shaved nearly 10 percent off the Dow.

"Many people feel the probability of the Fed tighting has been reduced," said Douglas Cliggott, U.S. equity strategist at J.P. Morgan. "Our view is it's a bit premature to move in that direction." The Fed's next policy meeting is on May 20.

The Treasury's benchmark 30-year bond was up 1-18/32 in late trading, its yield dropping to 6.98 percent from Monday's close at 7.11 percent. The long bond had not closed below 7.0 percent since March 26.
The lower bond yields are making stocks more attractive, said Jonathan Dodd, technical analyst at Dean Witter. "It's given people some room to play the market." he said.
The market's next economic hurdle comes on Wednesday with a report on U.S. first-quarter gross domestic product, due to be released at 0830 EDT (1230 GMT).

Yet some analysts said Tuesday's rally was strong evidence that Wall Street's retreat may have ended. "We will get pauses to refresh, but I think the correction is over," said Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards and Sons.

Among individual issues, International Business Machines Corp jumped eight to 158-3/8 after announcing that it added $3.5 billion to its stock buyback budget and increased its quarterly dividend by about 14 percent.
PepsiCo Inc jumped 3-1/8 to 34-3/8 after posting stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings.
Building on solid gains the previous session, shares of the interest rate-sensitive banks rose sharply.
Chase Manhattan Corp gained 2-3/4 to 90-1/2, Citicorp added 4-3/4 to 112, NationsBank Corp added 2-1/8 to 59-7/8, and Bank of New York jumped 2-3/4 to 39-7/8.

Shares of Bristol-Myers Squibb Co rose after it said it formed a consortium with Affymetrix Inc and Millennium Pharmaceuticals Inc to fund a five-year research program in functional genomics at the Whitehead Institute/MIT Center for Genome Research.
The program is intended to advance the development of gene-based technologies for research and health care.
Bristol-Myers rose 3-1/8 to 65-5/8, Affymetrix gained 1-1/2 to 22-1/4 and Millennium added 1-3/4 to 14-7/8.
The S&P 500 index rose 21.09 points to 794.05.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 25.60 points to 1242.63.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
